title: Lifeline pipe for the native lore binary, and the plugin installer's detached children (DEC-282 (a2) items 2 and 4)
description:
DEC-282 (a2) items 2 and 4, relayed by the leader 2026-11-19 from opum-doc origin/dev planning.json (DEC-282 outcome, opum-ai/opum-doc#1808, ODOC-634). Follows LCLI-797 (#734), which ships the wrapper's process-group shape and death-by-signal.
ITEM 2, lifeline: the wrapper holds the write end of a pipe that it passes to the native child. When the child reads EOF on it (the wrapper died by any signal including SIGKILL, or the caller killed the caller's group), the child kills its own group and exits. A pipe, not getppid()==1: portable and immediate, and macOS has no PDEATHSIG. Proof both ways: kill -9 on the wrapper, and kill -9 on the caller's group, each leaves no surviving native or grandchild process, plus a normal run unaffected. Needs a change in the native binary as well as bin/lore.cjs, so it is a DEC-182 (1) launcher-class build: sonnet or higher, opus security review, no DeepSeek.
ITEM 4: src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts:106 spawns detached children that escape either group design. Either stop detaching them, or track and kill them on shutdown and on lifeline EOF.
If this is not landed by the 0.15.0 pair cut, CHANGELOG.md states the residual (it already names both) and it ships in the next patch release.

acceptanceCriteria.text: kill -9 on the wrapper leaves no surviving native or grandchild process
kill -9 on the caller process group leaves no surviving native or grandchild process
a normal run is unaffected (argv, stdio, exit status)
agent-plugins.ts:106 detached children are no longer left running when lore is killed

implementationNotes:
OWED FROM THE #734 ROUND-4 REVIEW (reviewer verdict recorded verbatim on LCLI-797), carried here with the lifeline and the plugin installer's detached children.
F1, a pair-wide design gap routed to opum-doc by the leader: a nested quest native process can escape lore's sweep. lore spawns the npm quest.cjs wrapper with piped stdout and stderr, so quest.cjs finds no terminal and detaches its native child into its own session, outside lore's group; lore's kill(-lorepid, SIGKILL) reaches quest.cjs but not native quest. Deterministic where lore's sweep hits quest.cjs before it has forwarded (native lore killed by SIGKILL or OOM, and the exit-handler sweep after an uncaught exception); a race in the incident shape (SIGTERM to the wrapper reaches quest.cjs and native lore together, and the close-then-sweep can SIGKILL quest.cjs before its JS handler forwards, a window that widens under load). This contradicts DEC-282 (a2) item 1's grandchildren die with it, and the bin/lore.cjs docstring's 'A plain SIGTERM is fully handled'. Closed by quest's lifeline (QCLI-571). Until then CHANGELOG.md and the docstring should name it as a residual; the code was NOT changed for it, by the leader's instruction.
F5: test/bin-lore.test.ts SIGUSR1 witness is timing-dependent: dropping SIGUSR1 from NOT_RERAISED leaves the code and signal assertions unchanged, and only not.toContain('Debugger listening') catches it, which depends on the inspector printing before the loop drains and misses if port 9229 is busy. A deterministic witness would be a kills.cjs-style preload asserting no SIGUSR1 is sent to the wrapper's own pid.
F6: the SIGPIPE test passes against a mutant that drops SIGPIPE or SIGXFSZ from NOT_RERAISED, since Node ignores both; it guards behaviour and does not witness the change, and SIGXFSZ has no test. The exactly-once test is the real witness for N1.
F8: runLauncher does not pin stdin while startLauncher does; if Bun.spawnSync inherits a terminal stdin on a local run the exactly-once test takes the same-group branch and goes falsely red. Not a vacuous pass and not a CI concern.
F9: CHANGELOG.md, the 128+signal sentence sits inside the 'Also not covered' list as if it were an uncovered item.

#741 ROUND-1 REVIEW VERDICT, recorded verbatim (relayed by the leader 2026-11-21). Reviewer unit lore-cli-review-741, model claude-opus-5-5 (verified), reviewed head 1d2d73003b8bbaee9914351903fa981771af5b49, worktree .claude/worktrees/review-741-1d2d730. Round 2 pushed as 69c8250b, CI green (run 44925202195: 13 pass, 1 skipping).
VERDICT: REQUEST_CHANGES for opum-ai/lore-cli#741 (LCLI-799) at 1d2d7300. One blocking finding, a one-line doc fix; the code is sound.
Reviewed SHA: 1d2d73003b8bbaee9914351903fa981771af5b49
Model: claude-opus-5-5
Scope: read-only, no shell. I read the full 208-line diff, plus bin/lore.cjs, test/bin-lore.test.ts:160-480 and src/adapters/quest.ts, all at HEAD. I ran no tests or mutants.
FINDINGS
B1 (BLOCKING): bin/lore.cjs:131 still says "A plain SIGTERM is fully handled here." Round-4 finding 1 named this exact sentence as contradicted by the nested-quest escape. This PR adds a residual paragraph two lines below it. :136 says the TERM-then-KILL sweep closes only "most of the SIGTERM race", so the docstring now contradicts itself. Ruling item 1 is a documentation deliverable ("named ... in lore's docstring"). Scored on its weaker clause, it is half met while :131 stands. Fix: delete the sentence, or qualify it, e.g. "fully handled within lore's own group; see the stated residual below for nested quest".
N1 (non-blocking, read from code, not measured): on the uncaught-exception path, groupAlive's early exit probably never fires, so "an empty group costs no wait" is false there (docstring :181 and the CHANGELOG). On that path sweep() runs inside the `exit` handler while native lore is still the wrapper's live child. The SIGTERM at :191 kills it, and it becomes the wrapper's zombie. Node reaps children from libuv's SIGCHLD handling in the event loop, and the synchronous Atomics.wait loop at :193 blocks that loop. On Linux, kill(-pgid, 0) succeeds while a zombie is still in the group. So the loop runs the full 2 s and then always sends the (harmless) SIGKILL. Harmless in effect: the quest wrapper still gets its grace, and the zombie stops the pgid being reused during the wait. Unverified: how XNU's killpg treats zombies. The SIGKILL ≤1 assertion at test :415 cannot tell the two cases apart. Timing the existing uncaught-exception test (:296) on the ubuntu leg would confirm it: expect ≥2 s. Fix: soften the prose ("an empty group costs no wait on the close path"), or treat a group whose only member is the unreaped direct child as empty. On the close path Node has already reaped the child before 'close', so an empty group really is free there (the first SIGTERM throws ESRCH and the catch skips the rest).
N2 (non-blocking): the caller remedy at bin/lore.cjs:130-131 and in the CHANGELOG ("wait a few seconds, then SIGKILL") should give a number. Scenario: a forwarded TERM kills native lore, and the close-path sweep at :227 now waits up to 2 s on any group member that survives TERM. A caller that SIGKILLs the wrapper inside that window (`timeout -k 1s`, Python's terminate(); wait(1); kill()) stops the sweep before its SIGKILL leg. The surviving member is orphaned. The old SIGKILL-only close sweep had no such window. So this is a narrow regression for callers with a short grace, limited to members that ignore TERM. Say "wait more than 2 s, plus the child's own exit time". Note that a nested quest wrapper's grace runs concurrently, not added on.
N3 (non-blocking): test fidelity and hygiene of the new test, test/bin-lore.test.ts:424-480. (a) Possible false red. The fake quest wrapper writes its pid file (:431) before it registers its SIGTERM handler (:432). If the preload throws and the sweep's SIGTERM lands in that gap, the wrapper dies by default without forwarding, and native survives. The gap is tiny but it widens under load. It can only cause a false red, never a false pass. Fix: register the handler before writing the pid file. (b) The native-lore stub writes child.pid (:435 onward), but the pid is never read, pushed to `spawned`, or asserted dead. On a red run the stub (setInterval, own group) leaks past afterEach. Its death is never checked. (c) Only the exit-handler (uncaught-exception) path is witnessed. The close-path SIGTERM race, the other half of what item 3 claims to narrow, has no quest-child test. A second case that SIGTERMs the wrapper itself would cover it.
N4 (non-blocking): CHANGELOG.md:13 says "The exit sweep is TERM-then-KILL" with no scope. On a terminal (bin/lore.cjs:195) the sweep is still an immediate SIGKILL of the direct child. The docstring at :113 scopes this correctly; the CHANGELOG should say "off a terminal" too.
N5 (non-blocking, nit): the comment at test/bin-lore.test.ts:411-412 ("the stub's `sleep` dies of the TERM") is wrong. `kill -PIPE $$` ends the shell before `sleep` runs, so the group is already empty and the SIGTERM throws ESRCH. It appears in the log only because the preload logs before delegating to the real kill. The assertions are still right: removing the `swept` flag gives 2 SIGTERM lines, which goes red.
CHECKS
(1) Sweep correctness: clean apart from N1 and N2. Ordering is TERM, then a bounded poll, then a conditional KILL. The `swept` flag still caps it at one sweep. Every kill is inside a try, and ESRCH on the first TERM skips the rest. No exit path skips the sweep: a normal status exit goes through process.exit, then the exit handler, then the sweep; an uncaught exception goes through the exit handler, then the sweep; signal death goes through the sweep at :227, before reraise at :228. Only the spawnFailed paths skip it, as before. A synchronous sleep is correct in the exit handler, and Node allows Atomics.wait on the main thread. SWEEP_GRACE_MS and SLEEP at :233-235 are initialised before main() runs at :294, so there is no TDZ problem. Native lore installs no SIGTERM handler (I grepped src/), and the quest spawn at quest.ts:332 is a plain Bun.spawn. Nothing in native lore SIGKILLs the quest wrapper ahead of the grace. Pgid reuse: the probe runs every 20 ms and stops at the first ESRCH, so the reuse window stays roughly the old one. EPERM-as-alive can only cost the 2 s wait plus a failed KILL, never a kill of a foreign group.
(2) No regression against (a2)/(a3): the TTY branch (:195), the three-fd ownGroup rule (:147), reraise, and the NOT_RERAISED set are all byte-unchanged. On the signal-death path reraise is delayed by at most 2 s, and the signal it raises is the same.
(3) Test: not mocked, and not vacuous by reading. It uses real processes in the real shape: the fake quest wrapper is in lore's group, its native is detached into its own session, and the wrapper forwards TERM to -nat.pid. The preload throw makes the exit-handler sweep the only trigger. Against a SIGKILL-only sweep the fake wrapper dies before it can forward, and native (setInterval, reparented to init) survives, so the waitFor goes red. The earlier signal tests use a grandchild that ignores TERM, so they witness the SIGKILL escalation: a TERM-only mutant goes red there. Limits: it proves lore's half against a model of quest.cjs, not against the real quest.cjs. N3 lists the gaps.
(4) Residual: stated in the CHANGELOG (QCLI-571 named, SIGKILL/OOM of native lore named) and in the docstring at :133-139. Item 1 is not fully met until B1 is fixed.
(5) Tracker: LCLI-800 moves from tasks/ to completed/ (deletion plus addition, so no duplicate). The LCLI-797 and LCLI-799 notes are appended and none are lost. No other release blocker found.
NOT VERIFIED (no shell): No tests or mutants were run. "Red on the SIGKILL-only sweep, green on the change" is the writer's claim in LCLI-799's note. N1's zombie behaviour is reasoned from the code. Linux behaviour is from kernel semantics; macOS/XNU is unknown. I did not check the fake wrapper against the real bin/quest.cjs, including whether quest's own sweep finishes within lore's 2 s grace. Ruling item 1's quest-CHANGELOG half and item 2's QCLI-571 scheduling belong to quest-cli and cannot be checked from this repository. CI status of 1d2d7300 was not read.
ROUND-2 DISPOSITION (writer, 69c8250b): B1 qualified; N1 prose softened (close path free, exit-handler path may use the whole grace); N2 number given (more than 2 s plus the child's exit time); N3a handler registered before the pid file; N3b native-lore stub tracked and asserted dead; N4 CHANGELOG scoped to off a terminal; N5 comment corrected. N3c (a close-path SIGTERM quest-child test) deferred to a carrier after 0.15.1.

DEC-282 (a4) (opum-doc ODOC-610, relayed 2026-11-20), lore side, opum-ai/lore-cli#741 at 435689a2: item 3 landed in bin/lore.cjs (exit sweep is SIGTERM, up to 2 s grace, then SIGKILL; test red on the SIGKILL-only sweep, green on the change); item 1 stated in the docstring and the CHANGELOG as a residual until quest lifeline QCLI-571. The lifeline (this record, item 2) is still the close for a SIGKILL or OOM of native lore itself. QCLI-571 is scheduled first in the following patch release (quest-cli owns it, item 2).
